cards.front: What are classic causes of dilated cardiomyopathy?
cards.back: **Alcohol** abuse, **doxorubicin** (anthracyclines), **Coxsackie B** myocarditis, **Chagas disease** (*Trypanosoma cruzi*), **peripartum** cardiomyopathy, and **genetic** mutations (often autosomal dominant). The result is dilation of all four chambers with **systolic dysfunction**.
cards.back_pt: Abuso de **álcool**, **doxorrubicina** (antraciclinas), miocardite por **Coxsackie B**, **doença de Chagas** (*Trypanosoma cruzi*), cardiomiopatia **periparto** e mutações **genéticas** (geralmente autossômicas dominantes). O resultado é a dilatação das quatro câmaras com **disfunção sistólica**.

cards.front: In hypertrophic cardiomyopathy, which maneuvers make the murmur louder or softer, and why?
cards.back: The systolic murmur comes from **dynamic LVOT obstruction** by the septum and **systolic anterior motion** of the mitral valve. **Less preload** (Valsalva, standing) makes it **louder**. **More preload or afterload** (squatting, handgrip) makes it **softer**.
cards.back_pt: O sopro sistólico vem da **obstrução dinâmica da VSVE** pelo septo e do **movimento sistólico anterior** da valva mitral. **Menos pré-carga** (Valsalva, ortostatismo) deixa o sopro **mais intenso**. **Mais pré-carga ou pós-carga** (agachamento, handgrip) o deixa **menos intenso**.

cards.front: What are classic causes of restrictive cardiomyopathy?
cards.back: **Amyloidosis**, **sarcoidosis**, **hemochromatosis** (more often dilated), **Löffler endocarditis** (eosinophilic), **endomyocardial fibrosis**, and prior **radiation**. Stiff walls impair **diastolic filling**, and EF is often preserved. Amyloid classically gives **low ECG voltage** despite thick walls.
cards.back_pt: **Amiloidose**, **sarcoidose**, **hemocromatose** (mais comumente dilatada), **endocardite de Löffler** (eosinofílica), **endomiocardiofibrose** e **radioterapia** prévia. As paredes rígidas prejudicam o **enchimento diastólico**, e a FE costuma ser preservada. A amiloidose classicamente causa **baixa voltagem no ECG** apesar das paredes espessas.

cards.front: How does acute pericarditis present, and what are common causes?
cards.back: Sharp, pleuritic chest pain **relieved by sitting up and leaning forward**, a **pericardial friction rub**, and **diffuse ST elevation** with **PR depression**. Common causes: **viral** (Coxsackie B), post-MI (**Dressler syndrome**), uremia, and autoimmune disease.
cards.back_pt: Dor torácica pleurítica, em pontada, que **melhora ao sentar e inclinar o tronco para a frente**, **atrito pericárdico** e **supradesnivelamento difuso do ST** com **infradesnivelamento do PR**. Causas comuns: **viral** (Coxsackie B), pós-IAM (**síndrome de Dressler**), uremia e doenças autoimunes.

cards.front: What are the key exam findings and causes of constrictive pericarditis?
cards.back: A thick, fibrotic pericardium limits filling. Signs: **pericardial knock** (early diastolic sound), **Kussmaul sign** (JVP rises with inspiration), and edema or ascites. Causes: **tuberculosis** (most common in developing countries), prior **radiation**, and **cardiac surgery**.
cards.back_pt: Um pericárdio espesso e fibrótico limita o enchimento. Sinais: **knock pericárdico** (som protodiastólico), **sinal de Kussmaul** (aumento da pressão venosa jugular na inspiração) e edema ou ascite. Causas: **tuberculose** (a mais comum em países em desenvolvimento), **radioterapia** prévia e **cirurgia cardíaca**.

cards.front: Which organisms cause acute vs subacute infective endocarditis?
cards.back: **Acute**: *Staphylococcus aureus*; highly virulent, attacks **normal valves**, large destructive vegetations. **Subacute**: **viridans streptococci**; low virulence, small vegetations on **previously damaged valves**, often after **dental procedures**.
cards.back_pt: **Aguda**: *Staphylococcus aureus*; muito virulento, ataca **valvas normais**, vegetações grandes e destrutivas. **Subaguda**: **estreptococos do grupo viridans**; baixa virulência, vegetações pequenas em **valvas previamente lesadas**, frequentemente após **procedimentos odontológicos**.

cards.front: What are the peripheral signs of infective endocarditis?
cards.back: **Osler nodes**: painful nodules on finger and toe pads (immune complexes). **Janeway lesions**: painless macules on palms and soles (septic emboli). **Roth spots**: retinal hemorrhages with pale centers. **Splinter hemorrhages**: linear streaks under the nails.
cards.back_pt: **Nódulos de Osler**: nódulos dolorosos nas polpas dos dedos das mãos e dos pés (imunocomplexos). **Lesões de Janeway**: máculas indolores nas palmas e plantas (êmbolos sépticos). **Manchas de Roth**: hemorragias retinianas com centro pálido. **Hemorragias em estilhaço**: estrias lineares sob as unhas.

questions.stem: A 16-year-old boy faints while playing soccer. He recovers within a minute. His uncle died suddenly at age 28. Blood pressure is 118/72 mm Hg and pulse is 70/min. There is a harsh crescendo-decrescendo systolic murmur at the left lower sternal border. The murmur gets louder when he stands up and during the Valsalva maneuver, and softer when he squats. ECG shows left ventricular hypertrophy. Echocardiography shows a much thicker interventricular septum than free wall and systolic anterior motion of the mitral valve. A mutation in which protein most likely causes his condition?
questions.explanation: This is **hypertrophic cardiomyopathy**: asymmetric septal hypertrophy, a murmur that gets louder with less preload, and a family history of sudden death. It is usually **autosomal dominant** and caused by mutations in **sarcomere** proteins, most often β-myosin heavy chain or myosin-binding protein C; histology shows **myofiber disarray**. Plakophilin-2 (a desmosome protein) mutations cause arrhythmogenic right ventricular cardiomyopathy, which can also cause sudden death in young athletes, but it replaces right ventricular muscle with fat and fibrous tissue and does not cause septal hypertrophy or an outflow murmur.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **cardiomiopatia hipertrófica**: hipertrofia septal assimétrica, sopro que aumenta com menos pré-carga e história familiar de morte súbita. Geralmente é **autossômica dominante** e causada por mutações em proteínas do **sarcômero**, mais frequentemente a cadeia pesada da β-miosina ou a proteína C de ligação à miosina; a histologia mostra **desarranjo das miofibras**. Mutações da placofilina-2 (proteína do desmossomo) causam cardiomiopatia arritmogênica do ventrículo direito, que também pode causar morte súbita em atletas jovens, mas substitui o músculo do ventrículo direito por tecido fibroadiposo e não causa hipertrofia septal nem sopro de via de saída.

questions.stem: A 61-year-old man has 6 weeks of low-grade fever, night sweats, fatigue, and a 4-kg weight loss. He had a tooth extracted 2 months ago. He has known mitral valve prolapse with mitral regurgitation. Temperature is 38.1°C. There is a holosystolic murmur at the apex that is louder than on past exams. He has thin dark-red lines under several fingernails and small painful nodules on the pads of two fingers. Three sets of blood cultures grow gram-positive cocci in chains that are alpha-hemolytic, optochin-resistant, and bile-insoluble. Which feature of this organism best explains how it attaches to the damaged valve?
choices: Coagulase that converts fibrinogen to fibrin
Protein A that binds the Fc portion of IgG
Polysaccharide capsule that gives a positive quellung reaction
Dextran production that helps it stick to fibrin and platelet deposits
questions.explanation: This is **subacute endocarditis** caused by **viridans streptococci** (for example, *S. sanguinis*) after dental work, on a previously damaged valve. The splinter hemorrhages and **Osler nodes** (immune complex deposits) are peripheral signs. These bacteria make **dextran**, which helps them stick to the **fibrin and platelet deposits** that form on damaged valve surfaces. Coagulase and protein A belong to *S. aureus*, which causes acute endocarditis and appears as gram-positive cocci in clusters, not alpha-hemolytic chains.
questions.explanation_pt: Trata-se de **endocardite subaguda** causada por **estreptococos do grupo viridans** (por exemplo, *S. sanguinis*) após procedimento odontológico, em uma valva previamente lesada. As hemorragias em estilhaço e os **nódulos de Osler** (depósitos de imunocomplexos) são sinais periféricos. Essas bactérias produzem **dextrana**, que as ajuda a aderir aos **depósitos de fibrina e plaquetas** formados na superfície das valvas lesadas. A coagulase e a proteína A são fatores do *S. aureus*, que causa endocardite aguda e aparece como cocos gram-positivos em cachos, e não em cadeias alfa-hemolíticas.

questions.stem: A 67-year-old man has 8 months of worsening shortness of breath on exertion, leg swelling, and fatigue. He had surgery for carpal tunnel syndrome on both wrists 5 years ago. Blood pressure is 108/70 mm Hg. Jugular venous pressure is high and rises further with inspiration. ECG shows low QRS voltage in all leads. Echocardiography shows thick ventricular walls, normal-sized ventricular cavities, enlarged atria, and a left ventricular ejection fraction of 55%. Which is the most likely cause of his heart disease?
choices: Extracellular amyloid deposition in the myocardium
questions.explanation: Thick walls with **low ECG voltage**, a preserved EF, large atria and poor filling point to **restrictive cardiomyopathy** from **amyloidosis**; bilateral carpal tunnel syndrome is a common early clue. Hypertensive LVH also thickens the walls, but there the muscle itself is thick, so ECG voltage is usually high, not low. Alcohol, Coxsackie B myocarditis and thiamine deficiency cause **dilated** cardiomyopathy, with large chambers rather than thick walls.
questions.explanation_pt: Paredes espessas com **baixa voltagem no ECG**, FE preservada, átrios aumentados e enchimento ruim indicam **cardiomiopatia restritiva** por **amiloidose**; a síndrome do túnel do carpo bilateral é uma pista precoce comum. A HVE hipertensiva também espessa as paredes, mas nela o próprio músculo está espesso, então a voltagem do ECG costuma ser alta, e não baixa. Álcool, miocardite por Coxsackie B e deficiência de tiamina causam cardiomiopatia **dilatada**, com câmaras aumentadas e não paredes espessas.

notes.title: Cardiomyopathies, pericardial disease and endocarditis
notes.body_md:
## Cardiomyopathies

- **Dilated**: large chambers and **systolic dysfunction**. Causes: alcohol, doxorubicin, Coxsackie B, Chagas, peripartum, **wet beriberi** (thiamine), hemochromatosis, genetic.
- **Hypertrophic**: **autosomal dominant** sarcomere mutation; **asymmetric septal hypertrophy** with **myofiber disarray**. Dynamic LVOT obstruction. A classic cause of **sudden death in young athletes**.
- **Restrictive**: stiff walls, poor filling, EF often preserved. Causes: amyloidosis, sarcoidosis, hemochromatosis (more often dilated), Löffler endocarditis, radiation.

## Myocarditis and takotsubo

- **Myocarditis**: most often **viral** (Coxsackie B). Lymphocytic infiltrate with myocyte necrosis. It can progress to dilated cardiomyopathy.
- **Takotsubo**: sudden **apical ballooning** after intense emotional or physical stress, often in **postmenopausal women**. It looks like an MI, but there is no obstructive coronary disease. A catecholamine surge is the likely trigger.

## Pericardium

- **Acute pericarditis**: pain better when leaning forward, **friction rub**, diffuse ST elevation and PR depression.
- After MI: early fibrinous pericarditis (days) or **Dressler syndrome** (weeks; autoimmune).
- **Constrictive pericarditis**: **pericardial knock** and **Kussmaul sign**. Causes: TB, radiation, cardiac surgery.

## Infective endocarditis

- **Acute**: *S. aureus*, often on normal valves.
- **Subacute**: **viridans streptococci** on damaged valves, after dental work.
- **Prosthetic valves**: *S. epidermidis*.
- **Enterococci**: after **GI or urinary tract procedures**.
- ***S. gallolyticus*** (*S. bovis*): look for **colon cancer**.
- **Culture-negative**: think of the **HACEK** organisms.
- The **mitral valve** is involved most often.
- Signs: fever, new murmur, **Osler nodes**, **Janeway lesions**, **Roth spots**, splinter hemorrhages.

## Nonbacterial endocarditis

- **Marantic** (nonbacterial thrombotic): sterile vegetations in hypercoagulable states, especially **advanced cancer**.
- **Libman-Sacks**: sterile vegetations in **SLE**, on both surfaces of the valve, usually mitral.
notes.body_pt_md:
## Cardiomiopatias

- **Dilatada**: câmaras aumentadas e **disfunção sistólica**. Causas: álcool, doxorrubicina, Coxsackie B, Chagas, periparto, **beribéri úmido** (tiamina), hemocromatose, genética.
- **Hipertrófica**: mutação **autossômica dominante** do sarcômero; **hipertrofia septal assimétrica** com **desarranjo das miofibras**. Obstrução dinâmica da VSVE. Causa clássica de **morte súbita em atletas jovens**.
- **Restritiva**: paredes rígidas, enchimento ruim, FE geralmente preservada. Causas: amiloidose, sarcoidose, hemocromatose (mais comumente dilatada), endocardite de Löffler, radioterapia.

## Miocardite e takotsubo

- **Miocardite**: mais frequentemente **viral** (Coxsackie B). Infiltrado linfocitário com necrose de miócitos. Pode evoluir para cardiomiopatia dilatada.
- **Takotsubo**: **balonamento apical** súbito após estresse emocional ou físico intenso, geralmente em **mulheres na pós-menopausa**. Simula um IAM, mas não há doença coronariana obstrutiva. Uma descarga de catecolaminas é o provável gatilho.

## Pericárdio

- **Pericardite aguda**: dor que melhora ao inclinar o tronco para a frente, **atrito pericárdico**, supradesnivelamento difuso do ST e infradesnivelamento do PR.
- Após IAM: pericardite fibrinosa precoce (dias) ou **síndrome de Dressler** (semanas; autoimune).
- **Pericardite constritiva**: **knock pericárdico** e **sinal de Kussmaul**. Causas: tuberculose, radioterapia, cirurgia cardíaca.

## Endocardite infecciosa

- **Aguda**: *S. aureus*, frequentemente em valvas normais.
- **Subaguda**: **estreptococos do grupo viridans** em valvas lesadas, após procedimento odontológico.
- **Próteses valvares**: *S. epidermidis*.
- **Enterococos**: após **procedimentos gastrointestinais ou urinários**.
- ***S. gallolyticus*** (*S. bovis*): investigar **câncer de cólon**.
- **Hemocultura negativa**: pensar nos organismos do grupo **HACEK**.
- A **valva mitral** é a mais acometida.
- Sinais: febre, sopro novo, **nódulos de Osler**, **lesões de Janeway**, **manchas de Roth**, hemorragias em estilhaço.

## Endocardite não bacteriana

- **Marântica** (trombótica não bacteriana): vegetações estéreis em estados de hipercoagulabilidade, especialmente **câncer avançado**.
- **Libman-Sacks**: vegetações estéreis no **LES**, nas duas faces da valva, geralmente mitral.
